data.title: Carlos Slim Helu Discloses 6.5% Stake in BRASKEM SA
data.description:
Carlos Slim Helu Discloses 6.5% Stake in BRASKEM SA

Carlos Slim Helu and related reporting persons disclosed beneficial ownership of a 6.5% stake in BRASKEM SA’s Class A preferred shares, held through American depositary shares. They filed the Schedule 13D on November 6, 2026, using the company’s June 30 share count to calculate their combined stake. The group says it bought the shares for investment, not to change or influence control of BRASKEM SA.

Investor Intent

The group says it has no current plan to change BRASKEM SA’s business or control. It will review its investment and could discuss the company with management, directors or other shareholders, or propose changes to its capitalization, board or operations. The group also says it may buy or sell shares in the future.

Investor's Background

Carlos Slim Helu is a Mexican businessman and the lead individual in a group that includes members of his family, Control Empresarial and two Mexican foundations. A Mexican trust that benefits the Slim family owns all of Control Empresarial’s voting securities. The filing says boards with Slim family members in the majority make investment decisions for Fundacion Carlos Slim and Fundacion Telmex.

Original SEC Filing: BRASKEM SA [ BAK ] - SCHEDULE 13D - Nov. 06, 2026

data.title: Brent crude caps biggest weekly drop since pandemic as war premium begins to unwind
data.description:
Crude oil futures finished little changed Friday but Brent crude ended with its largest weekly loss since the COVID-19 pandemic, after heavy losses suffered by Republicans in the U.S. midterm elections raised expectations that the Trump administration will pursue a diplomatic solution to the conflict with Iran.

This week saw "the reversal of the substantial risk premium that had accrued across September and October despite resilient Middle East flows and rapidly normalizing global oil balances," Macquarie energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note.

Previous worries over a potential escalation in the Middle East have "given way to a renewed diplomatic push, less hawkish rhetoric from Trump, and apparent Republican introspection about the war in the aftermath of the midterms," Chancellor wrote.

Bloomberg reported Friday that the U.S. and Iran have moved closer to a potential breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Iran showing a willingness to discuss issues related to its nuclear program that were previously off the table.

Iran is studying proposals related to its atomic activities that were presented by chief mediator Qatar, and President Trump recently spoke by phone with Qatar's leader about efforts to de-escalate tensions, according to the report.

Physical oil prices are also signaling an easing in global supply conditions, and analysts at J.P. Morgan said this week that the global oil market is moving back into surplus as Middle Eastern exports recover and demand weakens.

Global supply exceeded demand by 1.1M bbl/day in September and widened to 1.4M bbl/day in October, while Middle Eastern oil exports recovered to 20.7M bbl/day in October from a low of 9.8M bbl/day in March during the first month of the war, the bank estimated.

Global oil demand has declined by 3.3M bbl/day since the conflict began, JPM also said, reflecting the impact of higher fuel prices and supply disruptions.

Nevertheless, the recovery in oil flows from the Middle East remains at risk due to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea export route.

A Greek ship manager said a seafarer was killed in a November 5 explosion on an oil products tanker in the Persian Gulf, believed to have been caused by a missile attack.

Data from U.K. maritime security agency UKMTO suggested that attacks on oil-carrying ships are still running at close to a record pace.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude for December delivery edged up 0.3% to $90.83/bbl and front-month Brent crude for December delivery gained $0.03 to $98.32/bbl.

For the full week, U.S. crude plunged 12.7%, its biggest one week percentage decline since the week ending April 17, and Brent crude sank 13.3%, its largest one week percentage loss since the week ending April 24, 2020.

U.S. natural gas futures gained as some cooler weather entered into the latest weather forecasts, lifting the front-month Nymex contract for December delivery up 1.7% to $2.998/MMBtu, its best settlement value since October 19; for the week, U.S. natgas gained 3.4%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF , tumbled 12% this week.

data.title: Good Purpose Investments Engages MCS Market Communication Services for Online Marketing Services
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Good Purpose Investments Inc. (FSE: 8BS) ("GPI" or the "Company") announces that it has engaged MCS Market Communication Services GmbH ("MCS") (address: Saarlandstraße 28, 58511 Lüdenscheid, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany; info@mcsmarket.de; +49 177 248 1220), for marketing services for an expected term of six month, commencing immediately. The term of the marketing services may be extended or shortened at the discretion of management depending on, amongst other things, the efficacy of the marketing services.

Pursuant to the engagement, MCS will provide a comprehensive suite of digital marketing services including, among other things: the development and management of digital campaigns, the creation of text materials; detailed keyword research and campaign optimization; creation of customized landing pages and coordination with online marketers; and placements across various online channels to improve reach and visibility. MCS will execute these services through online platforms using demographic, geographic, keyword, and interest-based targeting to reach relevant investor audiences.

The Company will pay a total fee of €500,000 (inclusive of advertising spend and an 18% agency fee) for the term, with the total fee being split into three payments throughout the term, with the first payment of €166,666 being paid immediately. MCS does not currently hold any securities of the Company and no securities-based compensation has been provided or is contemplated in connection with the engagement. MCS is a third-party marketing services provider and is at arm's length to the Company.

About Good Purpose Investments

Good Purpose Investments Inc. is a sustainability-focused company that acquires, develops, and scales environmentally aligned businesses operating across circular materials, sustainable manufacturing technologies, and next-generation consumer product categories. The Company aims to build a diversified portfolio of investments and internally developed businesses supported by shared infrastructure, commercial expertise, and centralized innovation capabilities. Its initial portfolio company is Waste2Wear, a wholly owned subsidiary of GPI and provider of circular textile and product solutions.

data.title: Voltas Appoints Sunil D’Souza As Chairman, Jayant Balan As MD
data.description:
Sunil D’Souza will succeed Noel Tata as chairman from 12 November, while Jayant Balan is set to take over as managing director in May 2027

Voltas has appointed Sunil D’Souza as its next chairman, succeeding Noel N. Tata, who will step down from the position on November 11, 2026. D’Souza’s appointment will take effect from 12 November, marking a leadership transition at the Tata Group’s air-conditioning and engineering company.

The decision was taken at a board meeting on 6 November. Noel Tata, who has been associated with Voltas’s board since 2003, will retire as chairman and director in accordance with Tata Group’s superannuation guidelines. The company has appointed him Chairman Emeritus from 12 November.

D’Souza, who is already a director on Voltas’s board, will assume the chairmanship while continuing as managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Consumer Products.

He took charge of Tata Consumer Products in April 2020. Before joining the company, D’Souza served as managing director of Whirlpool India for nearly five years, overseeing its operations in India and neighbouring markets.

He previously spent close to 15 years at PepsiCo, holding commercial and general management positions across India and other Asian markets, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia. He began his career at Hindustan Unilever in 1993, working in sales, after starting out as a service engineer at Siemens.

D’Souza holds a bachelor's degree in electronics and communications engineering from the University of Madras and a postgraduate management diploma from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta.

Separately, Voltas has announced a succession plan for its managing director position. Current managing director C.P. Mukundan Menon will retire on 24 May 2027.

Jayant Balan, currently heading Voltas’s room air-conditioner business, will succeed him from 25 May 2027, for a five-year term, subject to shareholder approval. He will serve as managing director designate until taking charge.

The company has also appointed Venkatesalu Palaniswamy, former managing director of Trent, as an additional non-independent, non-executive director with effect from 12 November.

The leadership changes come alongside Voltas’s latest quarterly performance. The company reported a 53.5 per cent increase in quarterly profit to Rs 526.4 million, while revenue rose 10.9 per cent to Rs 25.68 billion. Its unitary cooling products business, which includes room air conditioners, recorded 29 per cent revenue growth.

Noel Tata’s exit from Voltas’s chairmanship follows his retirement as vice chairman and director of jewellery maker Titan Company on 5 November.

data.title: Women’s Representation Must Become A Business Priority In Auto Sector: Madhukar Bhat
data.description:
Sansera Engineering CHRO Madhukar Bhat on advancing women in the automobile industry through inclusive policies, career opportunities and support for night shifts, transport and childcare

As the automotive industry works to improve gender diversity, organisations must look beyond hiring targets to address the structural and social barriers that limit women’s participation and career progression. Madhukar Bhat, Chief Human Resources Officer at Sansera Engineering Limited, discusses how companies can integrate gender diversity into business strategy and performance evaluations, while addressing challenges around night shifts, transportation, childcare and workplace infrastructure. He also highlights the role of industry bodies, skilling institutions and government support in creating a more inclusive workforce.

What are the biggest barriers to gender diversity in the automotive industry?

Traditionally, automobile manufacturing companies have been predominantly male-dominated. The assumption that only men can perform certain jobs, particularly in forging, machining and other labour-intensive areas, is gradually changing. However, these remain traditional challenges faced by most automobile manufacturing companies.

How do social norms affect women's participation in the workforce, and how can these challenges be addressed?

Initially, we faced challenges. However, once we started hiring women and their colleagues saw this happening, women's representation began to improve, making it easier to increase participation.

The main challenge is night-shift work, as automobile manufacturing companies operate 24x7. In rural areas, social and family pressures remain significant, as not every family is comfortable with women working night shifts. Day shifts are easier, but night shifts remain a challenge.

We are trying to reach out to families and explain the safety measures, transportation arrangements and basic facilities we provide. This may take more time.

In metropolitan areas, the situation is easier because many workers and employees stay in paying guest accommodation, and night shifts are common across several industries, including business process and information technology companies. This makes it relatively easier for women to work night shifts in metropolitan areas.

How can marriage and childbirth affect women's career growth and participation, particularly when workplace facilities and childcare support are inadequate?

Basic facilities are now commonly available, and providing them is also mandatory. However, transportation remains a challenge.

For example, a woman employee with a child may have to travel 10–15 kilometres to reach work. Bringing the child along in the transportation provided can be difficult. Even when workplace facilities are available, many women may not be able to bring their children to the office.

They may prefer a nearby childcare facility. One possible solution is to establish tie-ups with childcare facilities at different locations instead of providing facilities only at the workplace. While some employees may be able to bring their children to the office, others may need alternatives.

Providing reimbursement for childcare expenses could be a better alternative. The present labour code also provides for reimbursement, as permitted by the government. For instance, if an employee places her child in a nearby childcare facility, the company can reimburse the monthly expenses and establish an understanding with the union. We can reimburse these expenses legally, as permitted under the current provisions.

What concrete changes should the automotive sector prioritise over the next five years to improve gender diversity?

Instead of treating gender diversity as a separate diversity and inclusion initiative, we should make it part of the workforce strategy.

Just as companies establish performance metrics for quality, cost, products or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), women's representation should be included in the evaluation matrix for leaders, heads of departments and managers.

When women's representation becomes part of the organisational system and performance evaluation, it becomes an integral part of business operations. It should not remain a separate diversity and inclusion initiative but become part of the business strategy.

We have to move from treating diversity and inclusion as a standalone initiative to making it a business priority. This will help make such efforts more successful.

Many customers now expect this as well. The government has also introduced flexibility in the relevant provisions. Industry bodies such as APMA and GBL are helping companies by sharing best practices and solutions.

Every industry needs to make gender diversity an integral part of its business strategy.

What changes are needed in existing infrastructure and policies to improve women's participation in the automotive sector?

Transportation and housing are major challenges for smaller companies, and individual industries cannot address these issues independently.

The government can help by developing housing and transportation facilities in industrial areas, particularly transportation services for night-shift employees. This would help address some of the existing barriers.

Additionally, APMA and skilling organisations can help create a skilled talent pool and facilitate the sharing of available talent. They can also highlight the success stories of women in companies that have already made progress in this area. Showcasing these examples and sharing best practices can encourage other organisations to follow similar approaches.

I think these measures would help improve women's participation in the automotive sector.

Srijata Dey

BW Reporters The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld.
